edges.explanation: Confounding illustrates why correlation alone underdetermines a causal conclusion.
The need for discriminating research designs depends on recognizing plausible confounding alternatives.
The availability of stronger designs supports the qualified conclusion about when causal claims are warranted.
The final conclusion refines the opening limitation by distinguishing discovery or prediction from causal inference.
